Subject: Bluestone Payments — post-demo TCO readout & next steps

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the clear description of the fraud-detection use case and the throughput/latency constraints. Quick recap plus the cost levers we discussed and suggested next steps so your procurement and engineering teams can align.

Pain points you emphasized
- Real-time scoring across 1k TPS peak for auth flows (95th percentile latency budget: 200–250 ms).
- Current spend on hosted models ballooning with tokenized audit trails (long request contexts).
- Need for predictable month-to-month spend for budget forecasting; procurement requires a clear TCO for the next 12 months.

Goals we aligned on
- Proof-of-concept (4–6 week pilot) that keeps P95 <= 250 ms and demonstrates >2x reduction in per-auth token cost vs your current hosted vendor.
- Evidence of quality parity on the fraud scoring prompts (we'll use your labeled sample set).
- A documented rollback plan and a proposed reserved capacity profile if pilot KPIs are met.

Cost / TCO levers we recommended (short version)
1) Model selection & quantization: run a smaller causal model with int8 quant and fall back to a higher-cost variant for edge cases. Expect ~20–35% per-token cost drop from quant + model right-sizing.
2) Batching: group inference for near-synchronous scoring where safe (e.g., non-blocking risk scans). We estimated batching to reduce GPU token-hours by ~18–30% depending on burst profile.
3) KV/prefix caching: cache common prefixes and session-level context across auth flows — this reduces repeated context tokens and is high-impact for your long audit contexts.
4) Smart routing: route lower-risk traffic to cost-optimized pools and reserve high-SLA pools for critical auth decisions.
5) Commit/Reserved: moving to a small Dedicated pool (monthly commit) gives predictable unit price and ~15%–25% savings vs pure on-demand hosted.

Estimated TCO anchors (pilot baseline assumptions)
- Avg request size after prompt engineering: 180 tokens in, 40 tokens out
- 1,000 TPS sustained during business hours (with 3x peak bursts)
- With batching + cache + quantization, modeled token spend reduction: 30–45%
- High-level pilot monthly run-rate (modeling): $35k–$55k (hosted) vs $22k–$35k (dedicated + levers) — detailed workbook attached.

Next steps we propose
1) We will share the TCO workbook and a short demo log (attached) — please pass to procurement. (Action: Aditya — today)
2) Engineering sync to get sample dataset and confirm offline eval metrics (Action: Ben — this week).
3) Create a mutually agreed pilot scope & acceptance criteria doc (2–3 business days) so your PMs/procurement can sign off. (Action: Priyom — EOD Thu)
4) Optional: quick tabletop on SLA/fallback for compliance (ask from Samir) — we can schedule a 30-min slot next week.

Attachments: bluestone-token-econ-draft.pdf (TCO workbook, assumptions), redwood-demo-log-snippet.txt (sample latency/throughput from demo).

If that aligns, I'll kick off the workbook link to your procurement thread and Ben will reach out about dataset delivery.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side after internal triage:
- Procurement needs a month-by-month spreadsheet that separates fixed committed costs (reserved capacity) vs variable per-token charges. Can you break the workbook into those two buckets?
- For quality acceptance we need a 1k-sample holdout test where false positives do not increase by >2% relative to our current model. Can Ben and team confirm this is achievable with prompt/temperature tuning?
- On caching: we operate with session affinity; we want to understand risks if a cache miss happens during a high-risk auth. How would fallback work?

Hi Elena / Samir —

Quick answers to the technical asks:

1) Month-by-month separation: we've updated the workbook (linked below) with a dedicated sheet that isolates committed (Reserved pool) spend vs variable per-token usage. I'll export a clean PDF for procurement.

2) Quality acceptance (1k-sample): yes — with prompt engineering and a small temperature/penalty sweep we can meet the <=2% FP delta target in most cases. We'll run an offline ablation on your sample set and share the confusion matrix.

3) Cache miss fallback: Redwood's routing will detect cache-miss heuristics and (a) serve from a high-SLA model pool for that request, and (b) log the event and increment a short-lived retry window for critical auth flows. We'll document the exact behavior and latency delta — expectation: cache miss adds ~20–50 ms if served from the reserved pool; if a fallback to the high-SLA replica is needed expect +70–120 ms.

I'll set up a short eng session to onboard on the sample dataset and run the first offline eval. Proposed slots: Thu 4/9 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 4/10 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works?
